forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Rochdale Cabinet asked to approve £7.83m of high needs capital schemes, funded from two government allocations
news_drafts.lead:
Rochdale Council's Cabinet is asked on 24 November 2026 to approve the allocation and expenditure of £7,832,362 (£7.83m) of High Needs Provision Capital Programme funding. High needs is the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities.

The paper, High Needs Capital and Investment 2026, sets out the schemes in Appendix 1, Section 2B. Recommendation 2.2 asks Cabinet to approve them and to authorise their procurement under the council's Contract Procedure Rules and Financial Regulations. Recommendations 2.3 and 2.4 would delegate tender award and fit-out decisions to the Director of Children's Services, within the approved budget envelope.

Recommendation 2.1 asks Cabinet to note the Department for Education's high needs provision capital allocations. The allocation is £4,586,257 (£4.59m) for 2026-27, against £4,441,171 (£4.44m) for 2025-26. The paper describes these as the basis for the new programme. It does not say how the allocation is split between schemes beyond Appendix 1.

news_drafts.headline: Rochdale's pension asset improved by £18.3m but accounting rules prevent it showing in accounts
news_drafts.lead: Rochdale's latest actuarial valuation of its pension fund shows a net asset that has improved by £18.3 million, the Audit and Governance Committee heard on 24 September. However, accounting standards (IFRIC 14) impose an asset ceiling that limits the recognised net pension asset on the council's balance sheet to nil. The improvement therefore does not flow through to the financial statements. The auditors also identified and the council corrected a misstatement in which £14.75 million of Public Works Loan Board loans had been classified as short-term borrowing rather than long-term, which changes the council's debt maturity profile and refinancing schedule. The auditors said they were awaiting final responses on valuations of land and buildings, investment properties including the Manchester Airport shareholding, and pension fund assurance, but anticipate issuing an unqualified audit opinion once these matters are resolved.

findings.headline: The DfE published a schools white paper in February 2026 and consulted on SEN reforms that prioritise mainstream inclusion.
findings.detail: Paragraph 5.4 says the white paper proposes additional support bases and specialist bases, and that specialist bases re-label SEN units and resourced provisions. Paragraph 1.3 says the DfE is suggesting that mainstream inclusion be prioritised.
findings.matters: Changes to DfE SEND policy can alter which capital schemes qualify for High Needs funding, which affects any council's programme.
findings.figures: No figures are given for the reforms.
findings.quote: In February 2026 the Department for Education published a school’s white paper

findings.headline: The DfE High Needs Provision Capital allocation is £ 4,586,257 for 2026-27, against £ 4,441,171 for 2025-26.
findings.detail: Recommendation 2.1 notes the two allocations, which are the basis for the new programme. The paper does not say how the allocation is split between schemes beyond Appendix 1.
findings.matters: The year-on-year DfE allocation sets the envelope within which other councils must fund their own SEN capital schemes.

findings.headline: Two satellite schools are operating from commercially leased buildings and need re-provision of specially designed accommodation.
findings.detail: Paragraph 5.3 states that the Raise Rochdale and Redwood satellite schools are in commercially leased buildings and that there is a significant financial need to re-provide specially designed accommodation. The cost update was reported to Cabinet in June 2026, and this paper does not restate it.
findings.matters: Leased accommodation for SEN provision is a recurring revenue and capital exposure that other councils with satellite or alternative provision may also face.
findings.figures: No figure for the satellite school costs is given in this paper.
findings.quote: In both cases the schools are currently operating out of commercially leased buildings

findings.headline: Seven previously approved projects are reported as completed, including five mainstream SEN schemes.
findings.detail: Paragraph 5.6 lists Boarshaw Primary SEN unit, Springside SEN unit (now moved to Littleborough CP), Shawclough Primary SEN unit, Deeplish Primary resourced provision, and Norden Academy SEN unit as completed mainstream schemes. It also lists the Oak Haven classroom accommodation and the Redwood sixth form vocational catering hub as completed, and says SEN adaptations to Belfield CP were funded.
findings.matters: Completion records on named schemes let a finance officer compare delivery against the approved budgets and timelines of their own SEN capital programme.
findings.figures: Seven completed projects; five of them mainstream SEN schemes.
findings.quote: Projects previously approved and now completed, detailed in appendix 1

findings.headline: The SEN hub programme has created an additional 199 SEN places to date.
findings.detail: Paragraph 5.10 reports the cumulative places delivered through the SEN hub programme, which Rochdale launched in 2023. The paper does not give a target for the programme.
findings.matters: A count of delivered places from a named programme gives other councils a benchmark for what a mainstream SEN hub programme produces.
findings.quote: To date the SEN hub programme has created an additional 199 SEN places
